Contributor correction notice for `e086568649de35370209c8067ca2fdb8834979a6`: please hold the merge. A deterministic check found a missing completion-order case.

In `shell_window/capture.rs`, `complete()` queues the result and clears `in_flight`. If this occurs after the frame drains events, a second waiting request makes `due()` return true. `begin()` then replaces the shot flag. The next drain rejects the first result because its flag no longer matches. A failed capture can thus remain at `copying`; a successful capture can lose its clipboard event.

The check used the unchanged production `complete`, `due`, `begin` and `drain_events` code with a real wgpu device. The outer report consumer was a stub. It produced:

```text
completion queued; busy=true; due=true
after actual begin and drain: events=0; status=copying; busy=true
```

This is a deterministic ordering check, not a physical device-loss test. The five existing capture tests and 12 report tests pass but do not cover this order.

The bounded correction must prevent a new shot until the previous completion is consumed or times out. It also needs success and failure regression tests through the real consumers. No correction is published yet.
